scope: Fixed-time exponential evolution for fixed finite Fourier cutoffs of the free central-difference Dirac generator on the flat three-torus.

claims.claim: The continuum and central-difference Dirac mode generators are bounded continuous linear endomorphisms whose application agrees exactly with the Block 41 mode actions.
For every fixed Fourier mode, the central-minus-continuum generator converges in operator norm with O(h^2) residual.
The mode exponentials satisfy exact zero-time, additive-time, and opposite-time inverse identities.
For every fixed Fourier mode and fixed physical time, the lattice propagator converges in operator norm to the continuum propagator with O(h^2) residual.
For fixed finite Fourier support, the torus-L2 propagator residual decomposes exactly into orthogonal mode residuals and obeys an exact Parseval norm-square identity.
For fixed finite Fourier support and fixed time, propagated lattice packets converge strongly in torus L2 with O(h^2) residual.

nonclaims: No Hilbert-unitarity theorem for the mode exponentials.
No estimate uniform over a compact time interval.
No growing-cutoff or infinite-support convergence theorem.
No self-adjoint unbounded continuum Dirac operator, resolvent convergence, or cutoff-removal theorem.
No interacting or gauge-covariant propagator theorem.
interpretation: Universal Lean theorems under the displayed fixed-mode, fixed-finite-support, fixed-time, and positive-mesh hypotheses. No numerical computation substitutes for proof.
